question: Mohan bought some pens at the rate of ₹150/dozen. He sold them for ₹16 each. His profit percentage is ______%.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

CP of 1 dozen (12 pens) = ₹150

SP of 1 dozen (12 pens) = 16 × 12 = ₹192

Profit on 1 dozen = 192 − 150 = ₹42

Profit % = (42 ÷ 150) × 100 = 28%

**∴ The correct answer is 28%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost price of pens = ₹150 per dozen

Selling price of pens = ₹16 each

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 
 
 

 
 
 
 CP: ₹12.5
 SP: ₹16
 
• 
 

 Profit: + ₹3.5
 Profit % = (3.5 ÷ 12.5) × 100 = 28%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Number of pens in 1 dozen = 12

⇒ CP of 1 pen = 150 ÷ 12 = ₹12.5

⇒ SP of 1 pen = ₹16

⇒ Profit on 1 pen = 16 − 12.5 = ₹3.5

⇒ Profit % = (3.5 ÷ 12.5) × 100

⇒ Profit % = (35 ÷ 125) × 100 = 28%

**∴ The correct answer is 28%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). Selling Price = MP × (100 − Discount%) ÷ 100.

Successive Discount

For two successive discounts of a% and b%, the effective single discount is (a + b − ab ÷ 100)%.

Dishonest Dealer

When a dealer sells goods at CP but uses false weight, Profit% = (Error ÷ True Weight − Error) × 100.
